name: Sebastiano's
why: One of very few Sicilian delis in town, with a clear origin story and a sandwich Portland Monthly put on its best list. We know little about the newer Sellwood room, so atmosphere stays middling.
story: Daniel and Elise Gold opened Sebastiano's in Montavilla in 2020 after a trip to Sicily, then moved it to Sellwood in early 2024. Sandwiches come on focaccia baked in house, and the eggplant muffuletta made Portland Monthly's list of the city's best sandwiches.
tagline: Sicily-inspired deli baking its own focaccia
order: The eggplant muffuletta on house focaccia, plus a cannoli for the road.
practical: Part deli, part bakery, part Italian market
Daytime only: closed by 5 pm on its 2024 schedule
hours: Mon-Sat 9 am-5 pm (Bridgetown Bites, March 2024; not reconfirmed)
flags: Address confirmed at the Sellwood shop: the Portland Tribune inspection list published June 4, 2026 gives Sebastiano's at 8235 SE 13th Ave with a perfect score in May 2026. That is the latest dated sign it is open.

One location, not a chain: the original Montavilla shop (411 SE 81st) closed when it moved in 2023-24 (Bridgetown Bites). Portland Monthly reported a planned food cart in 2021 and a 2023 post mentioned a farmers market stand; I found no sign either still runs.
Hours are from a March 2024 post; confirm current hours.
The eggplant muffuletta honor dates from 2022 and the cannoli praise from 2024 coverage, both seen only in search snippets; check the current menu.
Owners' names and the Sicily-trip origin come from Wikipedia and a Jacobsen Salt interview seen in search results.
Discovery's 'Northwest take on the muffuletta with house-cured meats' line was not confirmed and is left out.

name: Kay's Bar
why: Ninety-plus years on one corner, a rumored ghost and real late hours carry the story and atmosphere marks. No single dish or drink stood out in what we found, so signature stays low.
story: Kay's dates to 1934, the year after Prohibition ended, and sits on the corner of Milwaukie and Bybee. Willamette Week judged it too polished to count as a dive and passed along rumors of a ghost. Its cocktails have drawn more praise than a neighborhood tavern strictly needs.
tagline: A 1934 corner tavern with a rumored ghost
order: A cocktail, ideally at the late-night happy hour, which starts at 10 pm Sunday to Wednesday and 11 pm Thursday to Saturday.
practical: 21 and over only, inside and out
Table service: sit down and order from your server
Parties of 8 or more need 24 hours' notice
Happy hour Mon-Fri 4-6 pm
hours: Mon-Wed 2 pm-midnight, Thu-Fri 2 pm-1 am, Sat noon-1 am, Sun noon-midnight (own site)
flags: Status unclear: no dated evidence it is open since Nov 2025. Confirm before approving.

No dated 2026 evidence I could open. The bar's own site shows current hours and online ordering; discovery reported a Feb 2026 Portland Tribune inspection listing, which I did not see. Confirm it is open.
Area: Wikipedia says Sellwood-Moreland and the bar calls itself a Sellwood institution; discovery had Westmoreland.
The ghost is reported as rumor in a 2016 Willamette Week guide. The cocktail praise is from Thrillist, seen via Wikipedia.
Founding year 1934 is from Wikipedia and the bar's own site.
Discovery's lead about happy hour nachos and fries (Portland Monthly) was not verified and is left out.

name: Bar Carlo
why: A solid neighborhood breakfast spot with real press, but we found little history and no standout dish beyond hearty scrambles, so the marks sit low. An August 2026 Axios story may lift the story mark once someone reads it.
story: Bar Carlo is a neighborhood cafe on Foster Road, in a room that used to hold a Russian restaurant. Breakfast is the reason to come, built around hearty scrambles.
tagline: Hearty scrambles in a former Russian restaurant
order: A scramble at breakfast, which is where the kitchen earns its reputation.
practical: On SE Foster Road near 64th Ave
hours: Breakfast 8 am-3 pm, closed Mondays (older Portland Mercury review; unconfirmed)
flags: Address: other sources give 6433 SE Foster Rd; the county inspection list in the Portland Tribune (Mar 3, 2026) prints 6439. I put 6433 in _address; same block either way.

Open evidence: perfect county inspection score in late Feb 2026 (Portland Tribune), plus an Axios Portland story dated Aug 24, 2026 whose URL says Bar Carlo went pay-what-you-can. Axios blocked my fetch, so that is not in the story. Worth reading: it may be the real hook.
Hours unconfirmed: the only non-directory hours come from an older Mercury review. Listings conflict, and some show evening hours.
The Mercury and Willamette Week reviews look years old, and I saw only search snippets of them.
'Since 2007', a Mexican-American menu and cash only appear only on directory or review-aggregator listings; left out.
Address corrected to 6433 SE Foster Rd (discovery had 6439 SE Foster Rd); coordinates from an OpenStreetMap address search.

name: HK Cafe
why: Long-praised dim sum and a famously busy room, but it is one of several dim sum halls on 82nd and we found no history to speak of, so uniqueness and story stay modest.
story: HK Cafe sits in Eastport Plaza on 82nd, and Willamette Week once named it the busiest of the avenue's dim sum spots. Dim sum runs all day, every day, and the shrimp har gow held up well enough to win praise as takeout in 2021.
tagline: Dim sum all day, every day on 82nd
order: The har gow. To dodge the crowd, aim for around 11 am or the 2 to 3 pm lull.
practical: In Eastport Plaza on SE 82nd Ave
Dim sum served all day
Does takeout
hours: Daily, dim sum all day (Portland Mercury, 2021); opening and closing times unconfirmed
flags: Status unclear: no dated evidence it is open since Nov 2025. Confirm before approving.

Open evidence is thin: no dated 2026 press I could open. Signs of life are an aggregator review from January 2026 and the online-ordering page noting dishes added in 2026 (neither citable). Discovery said a Portland Tribune inspection headline named HK Cafe in Oct 2026; I could not find it. Check it, including whether the score was low.

Own site (hkcafetogo.com) blocked my fetch, so hours are unconfirmed. 'Morning' rests on directory listings giving a 9:30 am daily opening and on Portland Monthly's 2022 best-breakfasts mention; evening hours are likely but unsourced.
Push carts: discovery and review sites describe carts circulating the room, but no source I could cite says so; left out of the story.
Story facts come from 2015 (Willamette Week) and 2021 (Portland Mercury) coverage; the busiest-on-82nd claim and the visit-timing tip are from 2015.
Area: Wikipedia and listings put it in Lents; discovery said Jade District. Address 4410 SE 82nd Ave matches across sources.

name: Roscoe's
why: Ordering good sushi from a shared kitchen while sitting in a former biker bar with 20 taps is a rare pairing, which carries uniqueness and signature. The room itself is a plain neighborhood dive, and the history we found is short: the biker-bar past and the arrangement since 2006.
story: Roscoe's went from 1990s biker bar to craft beer taproom, with about 20 taps that turn over fast. The same owner runs Miyamoto, the sushi restaurant next door, and the two share a kitchen, so nigiri can arrive with your pint. They have shared this SE Stark corner since 2006.
tagline: Old biker bar, 20 taps, sushi from next door
order: A spicy tuna roll or sea urchin nigiri from Miyamoto with whatever is fresh on tap. Miyamoto asks sushi eaters to try for a seat in its own dining room first, so tips reach its servers and chefs.
practical: Sushi comes from Miyamoto next door
Miyamoto asks you to try its dining room first
Own Cajun-inspired bar menu
hours: Open until about 2 am (PDX Today late-night roundup, likely 2024); WW's 2014 bar guide listed 11 am-2:30 am weekdays, noon-2:30 am weekends
flags: Current hours unconfirmed. The late close comes from an undated PDX Today late-night bar food roundup (its ID suggests late 2024) and WW's 2014 bar guide (to 2:30 am). The midday opening rests on the 2014 guide only.
The lead's back passage between the two bars rests only on a 2023 WW headline about secret tunnels. Left out of the story.
Address 8105 SE Stark St confirmed by WW, Jul 2026. Miyamoto is at 422 SE 81st Ave per the same piece.
Most recent dated coverage: Willamette Week Best of Portland, Jul 22 2026.

name: Kee's #Loaded Kitchen
why: Heaped soul food plates and a fried chicken seasoning that Eater said nothing in town matches carry signature and uniqueness, and the Cart of the Year win, the Netflix feature and the free meals in 2020 give it a real story. Atmosphere is a cart in a pod lot, often with a line.
story: Kiauna Nelson has cooked soul food from a cart in Northeast Portland since 2016, loading plates with fried chicken, catfish, brisket and mac and cheese. Willamette Week made it Cart of the Year in 2018, Netflix's Street Food featured it in 2022, and in 2020 community donations let her feed Black Portlanders for free.
tagline: Loaded soul food plates, Cart of the Year 2018
order: A loaded plate with the fried chicken, which gets a heavy spice rub before frying and a sweet, spicy seasoning dust after. Lines can get long, so arrive before opening and order to go.
practical: In the MLK Street Food pod on NE Martin Luther King Jr Blvd
Open until the food runs out
Lines can get long
hours: Afternoons from about 1 pm until the food runs out (KOIN, Aug 2023); current days unconfirmed
flags: Pod address confirmed: the MLK Street Food pod is at 3625 NE Martin Luther King Jr Blvd (Travel Portland pod listing and KOIN, which says the cart moved there from 5020 NE MLK).

Cart rules: in the MLK Street Food pod since Aug 2023 per KOIN, so about three years in place. Open evidence is the Portland Mercury Top 20 Food Carts list of Jul 9 2026 (seen via Wikipedia's citation and search results; the entry text itself was not read).
Hours are from 2023 and only show an afternoon start; current days and closing time unconfirmed.
Fried chicken detail and the arrive-early tip come from a 2021 Eater Portland list quoted on Wikipedia.
Heavy press (Netflix, WW Cart of the Year, Eater, Mercury, Travel Portland). Open-secret chosen because it is ten years old, not decades; reviewer may prefer local-legend.
Lead details not verified and left out: mac and Kees, pork chops, and Nelson growing up in Northeast Portland.

name: Abyssinian Kitchen
why: A well-regarded Ethiopian and Eritrean kitchen with all-teff injera and a family story, but Portland has several strong Ethiopian spots, so uniqueness sits in the 50s. We learned nothing concrete about the room, and it leans more polished than most places in the guide.
story: The owner and chef, a first-generation immigrant, put off opening a restaurant until her three children were grown. The Southeast Portland original closed during the pandemic in 2020, and the restaurant returned on NE Alberta in 2022. The injera is made entirely from teff, so it is gluten-free.
tagline: All-teff injera, back on Alberta since 2022
order: A spread of traditional stews on the all-teff injera. Ask your server about alternatives if you have dietary restrictions, and look at the cocktail list, which the Oregonian also praised.
practical: Gluten-free injera, 100% teff
Mostly traditional dishes; ask about dietary swaps
Full cocktail menu
flags: Hours unconfirmed. The own site gives none; an unattributed guide in search results listed Tue-Sat 5-9 pm, so evening-only is a best guess.

Fit check: WW called the original the most upscale Ethiopian restaurant in town (2016), and the Oregonian ranked it #23 of Portland's 40 best restaurants in 2025. Reviewer should decide whether it is too polished for the guide.
Open evidence: finalist for Best Ethiopian in WW's Best of Portland readers' poll, Jul 22 2026. The own site also notes a September vacation closure that reads as 2026 (reopening Wednesday Sept 16).
The 2020 closure and Aug 2022 return on Alberta come from Wikipedia and an Everout roundup seen in search results, not opened.
Owner's first name appears only on the own site, so it is left out. The family details (immigrant, waited until three children were grown) are from the own site only.
Atmosphere mark is low-confidence: no source described the Alberta room.

name: Tienda Santa Cruz
why: A solid neighborhood taqueria among many, lifted by its spot at the back of a working grocery and an avocado sauce people cross town for. We found little history beyond regulars coming for decades, so story stays low.
story: At the back of this red Mexican grocery in St. Johns, beyond the meat counter and the piñatas, is a taqueria with an open salsa bar. The signs promise a bakery and butcher too, but the avocado sauce is the reason to come. Regulars have poured it on burritos for decades.
tagline: A taqueria at the back of a Mexican grocery
order: Asada or al pastor tacos on doubled corn tortillas, heaped with onion and cilantro, then plenty of avocado sauce from the salsa bar. Don't try filling to-go containers at the bar; regulars notice.
practical: Taqueria is at the back of the grocery
Self-serve salsa bar
hours: Breakfast, lunch and dinner daily (Willamette Week, 2016 and 2019); exact times unconfirmed
flags: Exact hours unconfirmed. Only WW's 2016 and 2019 listings (breakfast through dinner daily); recent hours seen only on directories.
Open evidence: WW, May 12 2026, names the taqueria inside Tienda Santa Cruz among established St. Johns spots.
The decades-of-regulars detail is from the PDX Monthly St. Johns neighborhood guide; search showed it as January 2026 although the URL is dated 2021.
Taco details and salsa-bar etiquette come from a 2016 WW review. Prices left out as outdated.
Lead's pan dulce and bakery case not verified; the bakery rests only on the store's Panaderia signage (WW 2016). Travel Portland cheap eats mention from the lead not checked.

name: Pip's Original Doughnuts & Chai
why: Small doughnuts fried to order with house chai is a real point of difference in a doughnut-heavy city, and readers just voted it the best. Our sources say almost nothing about the room, and the story is a modest small-business one, not a decades-old legend.
story: Nate and Jamie Snell's shop on NE Fremont fries small doughnuts to order and pours house chai alongside. A second shop in Beaverton opened in 2023 and closed in December 2024, the owners citing rent and the economy, so Fremont is the only Pip's again. Willamette Week readers named it Portland's best doughnut in 2026.
tagline: Doughnuts fried to order, with house chai
order: A batch of the little doughnuts, fried to order, with raw honey and sea salt among them, and a house chai on the side.
practical: One location: the Beaverton shop closed in December 2024
Doughnuts are fried to order
hours: Daily 8 am-4 pm (Portland Monthly listing from 2014; current hours unconfirmed)
flags: Locations counted: one. The Beaverton shop (12400 SW Broadway) opened July 2023 and closed December 2024 per KOIN and the Bend Bulletin; no newer second location found.
Hours are from a 2014 Portland Monthly listing; current hours unconfirmed. The own site (pipsoriginal.com) refused the connection.

Page fetches of Wikipedia and Portland Monthly were blocked, so the owners, the Beaverton dates and fried-to-order rest on search-result snippets (KOIN, Bend Bulletin, Mashed). The 2026 poll win is confirmed on the Willamette Week page.
Raw honey and sea salt flavor comes from a Wikipedia-derived search snippet; menu not opened.
Opening year left out: Mashed says 2012, KOIN says about a decade before 2023.
Neighborhood: discovery says Cully; one listing puts it in Beaumont-Wilshire. Confirm.
Very well covered (Wikipedia article, readers' poll winner, Travel Portland doughnut list). Reviewer's call whether it is too famous for the guide.

name: El Sombrero Tapatio
why: A good family Mexican spot rather than a one-of-a-kind, lifted by a real story: a cook who worked her way up and recipes she brought from Mexico. We have nothing on the room and no hours, and every story fact comes from one profile.
story: Elvira Navarro came from Jalisco in the 1970s and worked her way up from busser to server to cook, the last ten years in this Parkrose kitchen. Relatives bought the restaurant, name and all, from a retiring owner, and it turns 25 in 2027. The mole and chile verde are recipes she brought from Mexico.
tagline: From busser to cook, with recipes from Mexico
order: The mole or the chile verde, both Elvira's family recipes, with a side of the refried beans. The birria began as a special and stayed on the menu because people kept asking for it.
practical: On NE Sandy Blvd in Parkrose
Birria is on the regular menu now, not just a special
flags: Hours unconfirmed: no own site or non-directory source gave them. when is set from the family's mention of a lunch rush; evening service is likely but unsourced.
Every story fact comes from one profile, printed in the Hollywood Star News (June 2026) and reprinted by Bridgetown Bites. That profile is also the open evidence.
Fame: open-secret by our two-outlet rule (Hollywood Star News plus the Bridgetown Bites reprint, and a KOIN item seen in search but not opened). Deep-cut is arguable since it is one article.
The year the family bought it is not given; 2002 is the original opening.
Some listings call it just El Sombrero; a delivery listing uses El Sombrero Tapatio Mexican Restaurant. Check the sign.
Staff named (Elvira Navarro) because the profile names her.

name: South Store Cafe
why: A century-old clapboard store turned cafe at a rural crossroads gives it more character than the menu, which is house-made pastries, soups and sandwiches with no named signature. The story is thin: little beyond the building's age and its past as a store.
story: This cafe fills a clapboard building more than a century old at the corner of Scholls Ferry Road and Highway 219, out in Tualatin Valley wine country. It was a store called the South Store before it became a cafe. Now it bakes pastries and makes soups and sandwiches in house for locals and commuters.
order: A house-made pastry and an espresso in the morning, or soup and a sandwich at lunch.
practical: At the corner of Scholls Ferry Road (OR 210) and OR 219
Breakfast and lunch
flags: Open: inspected in late June 2026 (Hillsboro News-Times roundup, Jul 16, 2026, read), score 84 with food-temperature violations noted.
Hours unconfirmed. Directories list Tue-Fri 9 am-2 pm and Sat-Sun 9 am-3 pm; not citable, use only as a lead.
The store-to-cafe history comes from one 2017 personal blog, which also said the owner had recently died. Current owners unknown.

Two of three sources are tourism-board listings (Travel Oregon, Explore Tualatin Valley). The Explore Tualatin Valley page now returns not found; its description (historic landmark, baked in house, commuter stop) is from the search snippet.
No signature dish found in a citable source, so order is general.
Discovery's lead about a 2025 brunch roundup ranking it ninth could not be found.
Unincorporated Scholls with a Hillsboro mailing address.

name: Fuller's Coffee Shop
why: The looping counters make it one of the last true diner rooms in town, and that room carries the marks. The food is a well-made standard breakfast rather than one singular dish, and the place now belongs to a restaurant group, not the Fullers.
story: Jack Fuller opened his coffee shop in Northeast Portland in 1947 and moved it to the corner of NW 9th and Davis in 1960. You sit on chrome stools at looping Formica counters, and the one-page menu is built around the classic breakfast plate: eggs, bacon, hash browns, toast.
tagline: Chrome stools on the same corner since 1960
order: The classic two-egg breakfast with bacon, hash browns and buttered toast, the plate the diner stakes its name on. It closes at 2 pm, so think breakfast or an early lunch.
practical: Counter seating on chrome stools
Breakfast and lunch only, closes at 2 pm
hours: Mon-Sat 7 am-2 pm, Sun 8 am-2 pm (own site)
flags: Founding vs. move date: not a real conflict. Fuller's opened in 1947 in Northeast Portland and moved to NW 9th and Davis in 1960 (Wikipedia, seen in search results, citations not checked). The own site confirms 1947 only and says nothing about the move.

No dated press since Nov 2025 seen. Open evidence is the own site's current hours plus site metadata showing its ordering links were updated Sep 2026. Discovery's Feb 2026 own-site announcement and July 2026 Silicon Florist mention were not seen this pass.
Discovery's 'same cheeseburger recipe since 1947' came only from an AI-rewritten travel site; left out.
Owned by Urban Restaurant Group (Wikipedia), which runs other restaurants; Fuller's itself is one location, so not a chain by our rule.
Counter-only seating is described by Wikipedia and the own site's photos and wording; worth a glance to confirm there are no tables.

name: Xin Ding Dumpling House
why: Two outlets rank its soup dumplings and Szechuan cooking with the best in the central city, which earns the signature mark. The room is a converted chain pub and the story is still young, so the other marks stay modest.
story: Xin Ding moved into the Old Town corner the Thirsty Lion pub abandoned in 2017, and the room is usually crowded. The soup dumplings rival any in the central city, but chef Keli Jiang's Szechuan cooking, like fish in hot gravy and dan dan noodles, is the deeper reason to come.
tagline: Soup dumplings where an Old Town pub once poured
order: The handmade pork xiao long bao, then a Szechuan plate such as the fish in hot gravy or the dan dan noodles.
practical: Big dining room that fills up
Second location in Sellwood
hours: Lunch 11 am-2:30 pm and dinner 4:30-9 pm (Portland Mercury, Dec 2023), with Fri-Sat service until 2 am (Willamette Week, July 2024); current hours unconfirmed
flags: Late hours (until 2 am Fri-Sat) come only from Willamette Week, July 2024; a Dec 2023 Portland Mercury listing showed 9 pm closes. 'late' left off until current hours are confirmed.
Most recent dated coverage: Willamette Week, Jan 2026, which mentions the new Sellwood offshoot. Discovery's Feb 2026 Hoodline mention was not seen.

Location count: Old Town plus Sellwood (7135 SE Milwaukie Ave per a WhatNow liquor-license item). WhatNow also reported a third location under construction. Three is under our chain line; recheck if a fourth appears. A MapQuest page shows the Sellwood shop as closed (directory, unverified).
Not a hole-in-the-wall: a large room in a former chain pub, open since 2023.
Chef Keli Jiang is named by Willamette Week. Pork-and-shrimp dumpling detail from the Portland Mercury review seen in search results only.

name: Stepping Stone Cafe
why: The Mancakes and the house attitude are real draws and carry the signature mark. The history is thin in what we could source, and we found nothing solid on the room or its age.
story: This Northwest diner's house motto makes clear they are doing you a favor by feeding you, and the attitude is part of the deal. Its Mancakes, pancakes as wide as the plate, got it onto Man v. Food.
tagline: Plate-wide Mancakes and a diner with attitude
order: The Mancakes, pancakes the size of the plate. It closes at 3 pm, so come for breakfast.
practical: Closes at 3 pm daily
flags: Status unclear: no dated evidence it is open since Nov 2025. Confirm before approving.

Open status uncertain, please confirm before approving: no dated evidence since Nov 2025 found. The own site is live with daily 7 am-3 pm hours (undated), while Groupon and MapQuest pages show it as closed (unclear if permanent). Discovery cited Travel Portland's Slabtown guide revised in 2026, which I could not open.
Discovery's 1948 soda-fountain origin was not found in any source; left out.
Mancakes and the Man v. Food appearance rest on search results (PDX Monthly, Willamette Week Cheap Eats 2011); those pages were not opened.
Own site still says breakfast, lunch, dinner and drinks but lists 3 pm closes; pre-pandemic late nights appear to be gone.
Most recent dated press seen is Willamette Week, 2011.

name: Escape From New York Pizza
why: Being Portland's first slice shop, still run by its founder after four decades, drives the story mark. New York slices are common in town now, which holds uniqueness in the 60s.
story: Phil Geffner and his sister Lauren opened Escape in 1983, and it was the first place in Portland to sell pizza by the slice. More than 40 years on, dough still gets tossed in the front window on NW 23rd, and staff and fans design its collectible T-shirts.
order: A slice, New York style: thin crust, big and floppy enough to fold. Keep an eye out for the newest staff-drawn T-shirt.
practical: Sold by the slice
Dough tossed in the front window
hours: Daily 11:30 am-11 pm per a 2024 listing seen in search results, likely Willamette Week's April 2024 roundup; not confirmed for 2026
flags: Open evidence: NW Examiner feature dated June 18, 2026, with the owner and staff at work.
Hours of 11:30 am-11 pm daily seen only in a search summary of a 2024 listing; 'late' left off until current hours are confirmed. If they still close at 11 pm, add 'late'.
Discovery's gruff-service angle was not sourced; left out.
Single Portland shop, unrelated to the San Francisco pizzeria of the same name. A longtime dough tosser is named in the NW Examiner piece but not in our copy.
